doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Lessons from age four and hearing Erroll Garner's Penthouse Serenade
summary: Her grandmother started her lessons at four, aimed at classical piano, until Erroll Garner's record turned her toward jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You began playing at four years old? You began lessons at four . . .
. . . years old, and this was at the prompting of your mother.
But I read that the primary goal was to make you a classical concert pianist.
Was this always your desire? Well, at four . . .

I don‘t know. I didn‘t know what I wanted, you see. I just know I wanted the music. It wasn‘t like, well, what direction? I just wanted to play the piano. But I had classical training in the beginning, and that‘s what I knew, you know. And I wanted to. I wanted to, to be a classical artist, but I don‘t know, something happened with it. Earl Garner [phonetic] came along and he kind of said, ―Ooh, ooh, ooh,‖ you know.
With Penthouse Serenade? Was that one of the many?
That‘s right. That was the first, that‘s right.
Would you say that was really the pivotal point for you, in terms of wanting to be a jazz musician?
I think so. I heard that; something happened, you know?
